content:
In recent years, Macs have become increasingly affordable. The starting price has dropped, you get more RAM and storage per dollar, and with the launch of the MacBook Neo, Apple has for the first time started to become one of the best-value options on the market.

Unfortunately, Apple has hiked prices significantly due to the ongoing memory shortage. Macs are not as attractive as they once were, but there are still solid deals out there — if you need a new computer, I would still say a Mac right now is a good choice compared with the rest of the PC market.

MacBook Air

Up until the MacBook Neo launched, the MacBook Air was the entry-level option in Apple's laptop lineup. While the MacBook Neo makes its value proposition a little more complicated, I would still say that if you want a better experience than the Neo but don't need anything high-end, the MacBook Air is an excellent laptop.

MagSafe, a P3 wide color gamut display, Center Stage on the webcam, and longer battery life are just some of the highlights of the MacBook Air. It also comes in a 15-inch size, unlike the MacBook Neo which only comes in 13 inches.

MacBook Neo

This product doesn't need a long explanation — the MacBook Neo is Apple's first affordable MacBook, with a starting price of just $699.

Compared with the MacBook Air mentioned above, there are some definite trade-offs, but at this price it's still an incredible deal. The build quality, display clarity, and macOS experience are largely uncompromised. Sure, you have to accept the slower A18 Pro chip (but honestly, it's not bad at all), fewer ports, and 8GB of RAM, but that's perfectly reasonable at this price. It also comes in fun colors like Citrus, Blush, and Indigo.

Right now there aren't any significant retail discounts on the MacBook Neo, but Apple does offer a refurbished version that saves you between $100 and $120 compared to retail. Apple refurbished products come with the same one-year warranty, are like new, and have every major component replaced. There will be no scratches or battery degradation issues.

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $689 at Amazon (save $10)
  • MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB RAM, Touch ID — $799 at Amazon
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $599 at Apple Store
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB RAM, Touch ID — $679 at Apple Store

MacBook Pro

The MacBook Pro is the top-tier model in the lineup. You get the best of the best, but there's one important caveat. Apple is reportedly redesigning the high-end MacBook Pros later this year with OLED displays, touch capabilities, and a thinner design.

That redesign, however, is only coming with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips first — so if you're someone buying the base model with the M5 chip, you're absolutely fine buying a new MacBook right now. Even if you don't care about the redesign at all, because the M5 Pro and M5 Max are still fantastic new chips.
